This High-End Papago Vans Transit Proves Rugged and Cozy Can Coexist in a Camper Van
25 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans
Naturally, the limited interior space in a camper van makes it impossible for you to fit all the comforts you have in a conventional home (unless you're living in a really small apartment). That said, a clever camper van design should be able to pack most luxuries people need – that's the case with the rig I'm checking out today.
What we have here is a conversion based on an AWD Ford Transit with an extended 148" wheelbase. It was created by Papago Vans, a Mesa, Arizona-based company specializing in transforming vans into adventure machines.
The vehicle's exterior is pretty indicative toward its "camper DNA" due to the various upgrades . First off, the van rides on Black Rhino wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires.
At the front, Papago Vans installed a CATuned bumper complete with two D-Ring recovery points and a hitch receiver. A CAtuned skidplate underneath, as well as a differential skid plate offer extra protection for the engine base. On the opposite end, you'll come across a spare tire carrier / ladder combo.
It's clear that the customer wants to take this van off the beaten path. Besides a suitable wheel and tire combo, they opted for a Van Compass Stage 3 Topo 2.0 suspension kit, which comes with Falcon rear shocks, a front lift kit, a rear mini leaf spring pack, and high clearance rear shock brackets.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Climbing on top of the vehicle was made easy thanks to an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) ladder permanently fixed on the driver's side. It leads to an FVC Safari roof rack holding two 200 W solar panels, an awning, and light pods on the sides; the customer will also fit a StarLink Mini antenna. The roof also has a Maxxair Deluxe vent fan and a Nomadic Cooling Co. A/C unit.
Other notable mods include Steelcraft side steps, CR Laurence half-slider windows, power and water connections, and flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow builders to fit beds in east to west arrangements instead of the standard north to south.
This rig's flares are finished in matte black, matching the rest of the exterior mods, and come with half-slider windows.
The interior has an open layout, meaning there's no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Thanks to the driver and passenger seat swivel bases, you can turn them around to face the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for soft blue laminated cabinetry, white shiplap walls, a stained wood ceiling, and wood-imitating LVP (luxury vinyl plank) flooring. The look is complemented by a bamboo countertop and various black accents, such as the kitchen hardware or the cabinet and drawer handles.
Dead ahead of the entrance, Papago Vans devised a two-person Alpine bench complete with a Lagun table mount. It's also mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned to face either the entrance or the cabin. The practical thing about it is that it can be folded flat into a tiny bed.
A cabinet above the bench hides the rig's "command center." It includes a touchscreen display that allows you to monitor and control the power system, as well as switches for a water heater, Wi-Fi router, shower drain, water pump, and a freeze protection system.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board cover and a filtered water faucet, a 700 W microwave oven, and an Isotherm fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans You'll have to use a portable stove for cooking. What's more, a Maxxair vent fan is perfectly positioned above to draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Two overhead cabinets, three drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen unit on the passenger side. The latter houses a Guzzle H2O water filtration system.
On the opposite side, a floor-to-ceiling storage unit integrates an overhead cabinet, a closet with hanging space, and four drawers.
Finally, the bedroom takes up the rear part of the living space. Comfort is ensured by a queen-size bed with a memory foam mattress, arranged side to side thanks to the flares I mentioned earlier.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans The bedroom also offers two reading lights, two overhead cabinets, charging points, a 32-inch TV attached to a wall swivel mount, and a Sirocco swivel fan. Moreover, a ceiling A/C unit can quickly cool the entire interior.
Like in most vans with fixed bed arrangements, the space underneath the bed was turned into a garage, accessible from both inside and outside the van. Besides offering a bunch of room for storage, it accommodates the utility systems in boxes on its sides.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 920 Ah Epoch lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter/charger.
Thanks to three charging sources, running out of battery will be a challenge, at least if you drive consistently and/or you keep the van in a sunny environment. You can use shore power, solar power , and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank with a heating pad and an electronic ball valve, a water heater, and an outdoor shower connection. Furthermore, an Espar heater that's tapped into the vehicle's fuel tank can make the interior nice and toasty when needed.
As you've already seen, there's no fixed bathroom inside the van. However, you can shower inside the van thanks to a Tetravan shower installed by the entrance. This space-saving solution has a folding aluminum pan and a water mixer that can be easily set up and used. To complete the shower, you must also attach a curtain to the ceiling.
All in all, Papago Vans has the ideal combo between rugged adventure capabilities and a cozy, well-equipped living space. If you want to adventure off-road and stay off-grid for a while, this is the perfect van to do it in.
